Map each node in the provided diagram to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change diagram text or layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (input-path):
Map n24-n37 key/mouse/paste/io writing. Return JSON partial line-numbered mappings.

     9	/// regardless of apprt in order to generate the proper terminal
    10	/// control sequences for a given key press.
    11	///

    13	/// as GLFW. In this case, the apprt should provide as much information
    14	/// as it can and it should be expected that the terminal behavior
    15	/// will not be totally correct.

    17	    /// The action: press, release, etc.
    18	    action: Action = .press,
    19	
    20	    /// The keycode of the physical key that was pressed. This is agnostic
    21	    /// to the layout. Layout-dependent matching can only be done via the
    22	    /// UTF-8 or unshifted codepoint.
    23	    key: Key = .unidentified,
    24	
    25	    /// Mods are the modifiers that are pressed.
    26	    mods: Mods = .{},
    27	
    28	    /// The mods that were consumed in order to generate the text
    29	    /// in utf8. This has the mods set that were consumed, so to
    30	    /// get the set of mods that are effective you must negate
    31	    /// mods with this.
    32	    ///

    34	    consumed_mods: Mods = .{},
    35	
    36	    /// Composing is true when this key event is part of a dead key
    37	    /// composition sequence and we're in the middle of it.
    38	    composing: bool = false,
    39	
    40	    /// The utf8 sequence that was generated by this key event.
    41	    /// This will be an empty string if there is no text generated.
    42	    /// If composing is true and this is non-empty, this is preedit
    43	    /// text.
    44	    utf8: []const u8 = "",
    45	
    46	    /// The codepoint for this key when it is unshifted. For example,
    47	    /// shift+a is "A" in UTF-8 but unshifted would provide 'a'.
    48	    unshifted_codepoint: u21 = 0,
    49	
    50	    /// Returns the effective modifiers for this event. The effective
    51	    /// modifiers are the mods that should be considered for keybindings.
    52	    pub fn effectiveMods(self: KeyEvent) Mods {
    53	        if (self.utf8.len == 0) return self.mods;
    54	        return self.mods.unset(self.consumed_mods);

    57	    /// Returns a unique hash for this key event to be used for tracking
    58	    /// uniquess specifically with bindings. This omits fields that are
    59	    /// irrelevant for bindings.

    30	    /// Terminal DEC mode 1036

    75	/// Encode the key event to the writer in the proper format given

    91	        opts,
    92	    ) else try legacy(
    93	        writer,
    94	        event,

    99	/// Perform Kitty keyboard protocol encoding of the key event.
   100	fn kitty(
   101	    writer: *std.Io.Writer,
   102	    event: key.KeyEvent,
   103	    opts: Options,
   104	) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
   105	    // This should never happen but we'll check anyway.
   106	    if (opts.kitty_flags.int() == 0) return try legacy(
   107	        writer,
   108	        event,
   109	        opts,
   110	    );
   111	
   112	    // We only processed "press" events unless report events is active
   113	    if (event.action == .release) {
   114	        if (!opts.kitty_flags.report_events) return;
   115	
   116	        // Enter, backspace, and tab do not report release events unless "report
   117	        // all" is set
   118	        if (!opts.kitty_flags.report_all) {
   119	            switch (event.key) {
   120	                .enter, .backspace, .tab => return,
   121	                else => {},
   122	            }
   123	        }
   124	    }
   125	
   126	    const all_mods = event.mods;
   127	    const effective_mods = event.effectiveMods();
   128	    const binding_mods = effective_mods.binding();
   129	
   130	    // Find the entry for this key in the kitty table.
   131	    const entry_: ?KittyEntry = entry: {
   132	        // Functional or predefined keys
   133	        for (kitty_entries) |entry| {
   134	            if (entry.key == event.key) break :entry entry;
   135	        }
   136	
   137	        // Otherwise, we use our unicode codepoint from UTF8. We
   138	        // always use the unshifted value.
   139	        if (event.unshifted_codepoint > 0) {
   140	            break :entry .{
   141	                .key = event.key,
   142	                .code = event.unshifted_codepoint,
   143	                .final = 'u',
   144	                .modifier = false,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        break :entry null;
   149	    };
   150	
   151	    preprocessing: {
   152	        // When composing, the only keys sent are plain modifiers.
   153	        if (event.composing) {
   154	            if (entry_) |entry| {
   155	                if (entry.modifier) break :preprocessing;
   156	            }
   157	
   158	            return;
   159	        }
   160	
   161	        // IME confirmation still sends an enter key so if we have enter
   162	        // and UTF8 text we just send it directly since we assume that is
   163	        // what's happening. See legacy()'s similar logic for more details
   164	        // on how to verify this.
   165	        if (event.utf8.len > 0) utf8: {
   166	            switch (event.key) {
   167	                else => {},
   168	                inline .enter, .backspace => |tag| {
   169	                    // See legacy for why we handle this way.
   170	                    if (isControlUtf8(event.utf8)) break :utf8;
   171	                    if (comptime tag == .backspace) return;
   172	                    return try writer.writeAll(event.utf8);

    25	/// to the pty to perform a paste of the input data.
    26	///
    27	/// The data can be either a `[]u8` or a `[]const u8`. If the data
    28	/// type is const then `EncodeError` may be returned. If the data type
    29	/// is mutable then this function can't return an error.

    32	/// data to be passed in without an allocation, since it is rare in normal
    33	/// use cases that the data will need to be modified. In the unlikely case
    34	/// data does need to be modified, the caller can make a mutable copy
    35	/// after seeing the error.

    37	/// The data is returned as a set of slices to limit allocations. The caller
    38	/// can combine the slices into a single buffer if desired.

    47	    []const u8 => Error![3][]const u8,
    48	    else => unreachable,

    51	    // a space (per xterm's behavior) for any text insertion method e.g.
    52	    // a paste, drag and drop, etc. These are copied directly from xterm's
    53	    // source.

    56	        0x08, // BS
    57	        0x05, // ENQ
    58	        0x04, // EOT
    59	        0x1B, // ESC
    60	        0x7F, // DEL
    61	
    62	        // These can be overridden by the running terminal program
    63	        // via tcsetattr, so they aren't totally safe to hardcode like
    64	        // this. In practice, I haven't seen modern programs change these
    65	        // and its a much bigger architectural change to pass these through
    66	        // so for now they're hardcoded.
    67	        0x03, // VINTR (Ctrl+C)
    68	        0x1C, // VQUIT (Ctrl+\)
    69	        0x15, // VKILL (Ctrl+U)
    70	        0x1A, // VSUSP (Ctrl+Z)
    71	        0x11, // VSTART (Ctrl+Q)
    72	        0x13, // VSTOP (Ctrl+S)
    73	        0x17, // VWERASE (Ctrl+W)
    74	        0x16, // VLNEXT (Ctrl+V)
    75	        0x12, // VREPRINT (Ctrl+R)

   130	/// exactly once: into the writer's buffer, where it is modified in place.
   131	/// This is the form to use when the data is const and the result is
   132	/// being assembled into a single buffer anyway.
   133	///
   134	/// The data is copied in chunks sized to the writer's buffer, so any
   135	/// writer works; a writer with less total capacity than the writer
   136	/// needs to hold at once reports `error.WriteFailed` as usual.
   137	///
   138	/// WARNING: The input data is not checked for safety. See `isSafe`
   139	/// and `isSafeWith` to check if the data is safe to paste.
   140	pub fn encodeWriter(
   141	    writer: *std.Io.Writer,
   142	    data: []const u8,
   143	    opts: Options,
   144	) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
   145	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_prefix);

   147	    // The byte transformations are position-independent, so the data
   148	    // can be copied and encoded chunk by chunk. The frame returned by
   149	    // encode is ignored since it's written around the whole data here.
   150	    var remaining = data;
   151	    while (remaining.len > 0) {
   152	        const dest = try writer.writableSliceGreedy(1);
   153	        const n = @min(dest.len, remaining.len);
   154	        @memcpy(dest[0..n], remaining[0..n]);
   155	        _ = encode(dest[0..n], opts);
   156	        writer.advance(n);
   157	        remaining = remaining[n..];
   158	    }
   159	
   160	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_suffix);
   161	}

   107	        writer,
   108	        event,
   109	        opts,
   110	    );

   112	    // We only processed "press" events unless report events is active
   113	    if (event.action == .release) {
   114	        if (!opts.kitty_flags.report_events) return;

   116	        // Enter, backspace, and tab do not report release events unless "report
   117	        // all" is set
   118	        if (!opts.kitty_flags.report_all) {
   119	            switch (event.key) {
   120	                .enter, .backspace, .tab => return,
   121	                else => {},
   122	            }

   126	    const all_mods = event.mods;
   127	    const effective_mods = event.effectiveMods();
   128	    const binding_mods = effective_mods.binding();

   130	    // Find the entry for this key in the kitty table.
   131	    const entry_: ?KittyEntry = entry: {
   132	        // Functional or predefined keys
   133	        for (kitty_entries) |entry| {
   134	            if (entry.key == event.key) break :entry entry;
   135	        }

   137	        // Otherwise, we use our unicode codepoint from UTF8. We
   138	        // always use the unshifted value.
   139	        if (event.unshifted_codepoint > 0) {

   141	                .key = event.key,
   142	                .code = event.unshifted_codepoint,
   143	                .final = 'u',
   144	                .modifier = false,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        break :entry null;
   149	    };

   152	        // When composing, the only keys sent are plain modifiers.
   153	        if (event.composing) {

   155	                if (entry.modifier) break :preprocessing;
   156	            }

   158	            return;
   159	        }

    24	/// Encode the given data for pasting. The resulting value can be written
    25	/// to the pty to perform a paste of the input data.
    26	///
    27	/// The data can be either a `[]u8` or a `[]const u8`. If the data
    28	/// type is const then `EncodeError` may be returned. If the data type
    29	/// is mutable then this function can't return an error.

    32	/// data to be passed in without an allocation, since it is rare in normal
    33	/// use cases that the data will need to be modified. In the unlikely case
    34	/// data does need to be modified, the caller can make a mutable copy
    35	/// after seeing the error.

    38	/// can combine the slices into a single buffer if desired.

    47	    []const u8 => Error![3][]const u8,
    48	    else => unreachable,
    49	} {

    51	    // a space (per xterm's behavior) for any text insertion method e.g.
    52	    // a paste, drag and drop, etc. These are copied directly from xterm's
    53	    // source.

    56	        0x08, // BS
    57	        0x05, // ENQ
    58	        0x04, // EOT
    59	        0x1B, // ESC
    60	        0x7F, // DEL
    61	
    62	        // These can be overridden by the running terminal program
    63	        // via tcsetattr, so they aren't totally safe to hardcode like
    64	        // this. In practice, I haven't seen modern programs change these
    65	        // and its a much bigger architectural change to pass these through
    66	        // so for now they're hardcoded.
    67	        0x03, // VINTR (Ctrl+C)
    68	        0x1C, // VQUIT (Ctrl+\)
    69	        0x15, // VKILL (Ctrl+U)
    70	        0x1A, // VSUSP (Ctrl+Z)
    71	        0x11, // VSTART (Ctrl+Q)
    72	        0x13, // VSTOP (Ctrl+S)
    73	        0x17, // VWERASE (Ctrl+W)
    74	        0x16, // VLNEXT (Ctrl+V)
    75	        0x12, // VREPRINT (Ctrl+R)
    76	        0x0F, // VDISCARD (Ctrl+O)

   130	/// exactly once: into the writer's buffer, where it is modified in place.
   131	/// This is the form to use when the data is const and the result is
   132	/// being assembled into a single buffer anyway.
   133	///
   134	/// The data is copied in chunks sized to the writer's buffer, so any
   135	/// writer works; a writer with less total capacity than the writer
   136	/// needs to hold at once reports `error.WriteFailed` as usual.
   137	///
   138	/// WARNING: The input data is not checked for safety. See `isSafe`
   139	/// and `isSafeWith` to check if the data is safe to paste.
   140	pub fn encodeWriter(
   141	    writer: *std.Io.Writer,
   142	    data: []const u8,
   143	    opts: Options,
   144	) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
   145	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_prefix);

   147	    // The byte transformations are position-independent, so the data
   148	    // can be copied and encoded chunk by chunk. The frame returned by
   149	    // encode is ignored since it's written around the whole data here.
   150	    var remaining = data;
   151	    while (remaining.len > 0) {
   152	        const dest = try writer.writableSliceGreedy(1);
   153	        const n = @min(dest.len, remaining.len);
   154	        @memcpy(dest[0..n], remaining[0..n]);
   155	        _ = encode(dest[0..n], opts);
   156	        writer.advance(n);
   157	        remaining = remaining[n..];
   158	    }
   159	
   160	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_suffix);
   161	}

    24	/// Encode the given data for pasting. The resulting value can be written
    25	/// to the pty to perform a paste of the input data.
    26	///
    27	/// The data can be either a `[]u8` or a `[]const u8`. If the data
    28	/// type is const then `EncodeError` may be returned. If the data type
    29	/// is mutable then this function can't return an error.
    30	///
    31	/// This slightly complex calling style allows for initially const
    32	/// data to be passed in without an allocation, since it is rare in normal
    33	/// use cases that the data will need to be modified. In the unlikely case
    34	/// data does need to be modified, the caller can make a mutable copy
    35	/// after seeing the error.

    37	/// The data is returned as a set of slices to limit allocations. The caller
    38	/// can combine the slices into a single buffer if desired.

    45	) switch (@TypeOf(data)) {
    46	    []u8 => [3][]const u8,
    47	    []const u8 => Error![3][]const u8,
    48	    else => unreachable,
    49	} {
    50	    // These are the set of byte values that are always replaced by
    51	    // a space (per xterm's behavior) for any text insertion method e.g.
    52	    // a paste, drag and drop, etc. These are copied directly from xterm's
    53	    // source.

    56	        0x08, // BS
    57	        0x05, // ENQ
    58	        0x04, // EOT
    59	        0x1B, // ESC
    60	        0x7F, // DEL
    61	
    62	        // These can be overridden by the running terminal program
    63	        // via tcsetattr, so they aren't totally safe to hardcode like
    64	        // this. In practice, I haven't seen modern programs change these
    65	        // and its a much bigger architectural change to pass these through
    66	        // so for now they're hardcoded.
    67	        0x03, // VINTR (Ctrl+C)
    68	        0x1C, // VQUIT (Ctrl+\)
    69	        0x15, // VKILL (Ctrl+U)
    70	        0x1A, // VSUSP (Ctrl+Z)
    71	        0x11, // VSTART (Ctrl+Q)
    72	        0x13, // VSTOP (Ctrl+S)
    73	        0x17, // VWERASE (Ctrl+W)
    74	        0x16, // VLNEXT (Ctrl+V)
    75	        0x12, // VREPRINT (Ctrl+R)
    76	        0x0F, // VDISCARD (Ctrl+O)

    86	    // from containing bytes that could be used to inject commands.

    88	        if (comptime !mutable) return Error.MutableRequired;

   128	/// the same transformation as `encode` (unsafe bytes replaced, bracketed

   130	/// exactly once: into the writer's buffer, where it is modified in place.
   131	/// This is the form to use when the data is const and the result is
   132	/// being assembled into a single buffer anyway.
   133	///
   134	/// The data is copied in chunks sized to the writer's buffer, so any
   135	/// writer works; a writer with less total capacity than the writer
   136	/// needs to hold at once reports `error.WriteFailed` as usual.
   137	///
   138	/// WARNING: The input data is not checked for safety. See `isSafe`
   139	/// and `isSafeWith` to check if the data is safe to paste.
   140	pub fn encodeWriter(
   141	    writer: *std.Io.Writer,
   142	    data: []const u8,
   143	    opts: Options,
   144	) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
   145	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_prefix);
   146	
   147	    // The byte transformations are position-independent, so the data
   148	    // can be copied and encoded chunk by chunk. The frame returned by
   149	    // encode is ignored since it's written around the whole data here.
   150	    var remaining = data;
   151	    while (remaining.len > 0) {
   152	        const dest = try writer.writableSliceGreedy(1);
   153	        const n = @min(dest.len, remaining.len);
   154	        @memcpy(dest[0..n], remaining[0..n]);
   155	        _ = encode(dest[0..n], opts);
   156	        writer.advance(n);
   157	        remaining = remaining[n..];
   158	    }
   159	
   160	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_suffix);
   161	}

    24	/// Encode the given data for pasting. The resulting value can be written
    25	/// to the pty to perform a paste of the input data.
    26	///
    27	/// The data can be either a `[]u8` or a `[]const u8`. If the data
    28	/// type is const then `EncodeError` may be returned. If the data type
    29	/// is mutable then this function can't return an error.
    30	///
    31	/// This slightly complex calling style allows for initially const
    32	/// data to be passed in without an allocation, since it is rare in normal
    33	/// use cases that the data will need to be modified. In the unlikely case
    34	/// data does need to be modified, the caller can make a mutable copy
    35	/// after seeing the error.
    36	///
    37	/// The data is returned as a set of slices to limit allocations. The caller
    38	/// can combine the slices into a single buffer if desired.

    41	/// function to check if the data is safe to paste.
    42	pub fn encode(
    43	    data: anytype,
    44	    opts: Options,
    45	) switch (@TypeOf(data)) {
    46	    []u8 => [3][]const u8,
    47	    []const u8 => Error![3][]const u8,
    48	    else => unreachable,
    49	} {
    50	    // These are the set of byte values that are always replaced by
    51	    // a space (per xterm's behavior) for any text insertion method e.g.
    52	    // a paste, drag and drop, etc. These are copied directly from xterm's
    53	    // source.

    55	        0x00, // NUL
    56	        0x08, // BS
    57	        0x05, // ENQ
    58	        0x04, // EOT
    59	        0x1B, // ESC
    60	        0x7F, // DEL
    61	
    62	        // These can be overridden by the running terminal program
    63	        // via tcsetattr, so they aren't totally safe to hardcode like
    64	        // this. In practice, I haven't seen modern programs change these
    65	        // and its a much bigger architectural change to pass these through
    66	        // so for now they're hardcoded.
    67	        0x03, // VINTR (Ctrl+C)
    68	        0x1C, // VQUIT (Ctrl+\)
    69	        0x15, // VKILL (Ctrl+U)
    70	        0x1A, // VSUSP (Ctrl+Z)
    71	        0x11, // VSTART (Ctrl+Q)
    72	        0x13, // VSTOP (Ctrl+S)
    73	        0x17, // VWERASE (Ctrl+W)
    74	        0x16, // VLNEXT (Ctrl+V)
    75	        0x12, // VREPRINT (Ctrl+R)
    76	        0x0F, // VDISCARD (Ctrl+O)
    77	    };

    79	    const mutable = @TypeOf(data) == []u8;

    81	    var result: [3][]const u8 = .{ "", data, "" };

    83	    // If we have any of the strip values, then we need to replace them

    86	    // from containing bytes that could be used to inject commands.
    87	    if (std.mem.indexOfAny(u8, data, strip) != null) {
    88	        if (comptime !mutable) return Error.MutableRequired;

    90	        while (std.mem.indexOfAny(
    91	            u8,
    92	            data[offset..],
    93	            strip,
    94	        )) |idx| {

    96	            data[offset] = ' ';

    98	        }

   127	/// Encode the given data for pasting directly into a writer. This is
   128	/// the same transformation as `encode` (unsafe bytes replaced, bracketed
   129	/// frame or newline conversion per `opts`) but the data is copied
   130	/// exactly once: into the writer's buffer, where it is modified in place.
   131	/// This is the form to use when the data is const and the result is
   132	/// being assembled into a single buffer anyway.
   133	///
   134	/// The data is copied in chunks sized to the writer's buffer, so any
   135	/// writer works; a writer with less total capacity than the writer
   136	/// needs to hold at once reports `error.WriteFailed` as usual.
   137	///
   138	/// WARNING: The input data is not checked for safety. See `isSafe`
   139	/// and `isSafeWith` to check if the data is safe to paste.
   140	pub fn encodeWriter(
   141	    writer: *std.Io.Writer,
   142	    data: []const u8,
   143	    opts: Options,
   144	) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
   145	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_prefix);
   146	
   147	    // The byte transformations are position-independent, so the data
   148	    // can be copied and encoded chunk by chunk. The frame returned by
   149	    // encode is ignored since it's written around the whole data here.
   150	    var remaining = data;
   151	    while (remaining.len > 0) {
   152	        const dest = try writer.writableSliceGreedy(1);
   153	        const n = @min(dest.len, remaining.len);
   154	        @memcpy(dest[0..n], remaining[0..n]);
   155	        _ = encode(dest[0..n], opts);
   156	        writer.advance(n);
   157	        remaining = remaining[n..];
   158	    }
   159	
   160	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_suffix);
   161	}

Map each node in the provided diagram to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change diagram text or layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (input-path):
Map n24-n37 key/mouse/paste/io writing. Return JSON partial line-numbered mappings.

     8	/// A generic key input event. This is the information that is necessary
     9	/// regardless of apprt in order to generate the proper terminal
    10	/// control sequences for a given key press.
    11	///
    12	/// Some apprts may not be able to provide all of this information, such
    13	/// as GLFW. In this case, the apprt should provide as much information
    14	/// as it can and it should be expected that the terminal behavior
    15	/// will not be totally correct.
    16	pub const KeyEvent = struct {
    17	    /// The action: press, release, etc.
    18	    action: Action = .press,
    19	
    20	    /// The keycode of the physical key that was pressed. This is agnostic
    21	    /// to the layout. Layout-dependent matching can only be done via the
    22	    /// UTF-8 or unshifted codepoint.
    23	    key: Key = .unidentified,
    24	
    25	    /// Mods are the modifiers that are pressed.
    26	    mods: Mods = .{},
    27	
    28	    /// The mods that were consumed in order to generate the text
    29	    /// in utf8. This has the mods set that were consumed, so to
    30	    /// get the set of mods that are effective you must negate
    31	    /// mods with this.
    32	    ///
    33	    /// This field is meaningless if utf8 is empty.
    34	    consumed_mods: Mods = .{},
    35	
    36	    /// Composing is true when this key event is part of a dead key
    37	    /// composition sequence and we're in the middle of it.
    38	    composing: bool = false,
    39	
    40	    /// The utf8 sequence that was generated by this key event.
    41	    /// This will be an empty string if there is no text generated.
    42	    /// If composing is true and this is non-empty, this is preedit
    43	    /// text.
    44	    utf8: []const u8 = "",
    45	
    46	    /// The codepoint for this key when it is unshifted. For example,
    47	    /// shift+a is "A" in UTF-8 but unshifted would provide 'a'.
    48	    unshifted_codepoint: u21 = 0,
    49	
    50	    /// Returns the effective modifiers for this event. The effective
    51	    /// modifiers are the mods that should be considered for keybindings.
    52	    pub fn effectiveMods(self: KeyEvent) Mods {
    53	        if (self.utf8.len == 0) return self.mods;
    54	        return self.mods.unset(self.consumed_mods);
    55	    }

    57	    /// Returns a unique hash for this key event to be used for tracking
    58	    /// uniquess specifically with bindings. This omits fields that are
    59	    /// irrelevant for bindings.
    60	    pub fn bindingHash(self: KeyEvent) u64 {
    61	        var hasher = std.hash.Wyhash.init(0);
    62	
    63	        // These are all the fields that are explicitly part of Trigger.
    64	        std.hash.autoHash(&hasher, self.key);
    65	        std.hash.autoHash(&hasher, self.unshifted_codepoint);

    73	        //
    74	        // We can add to this if there is other confusion.

    24	/// Encode the given data for pasting. The resulting value can be written
    25	/// to the pty to perform a paste of the input data.
    26	///
    27	/// The data can be either a `[]u8` or a `[]const u8`. If the data
    28	/// type is const then `EncodeError` may be returned. If the data type
    29	/// is mutable then this function can't return an error.
    30	///
    31	/// This slightly complex calling style allows for initially const
    32	/// data to be passed in without an allocation, since it is rare in normal
    33	/// use cases that the data will need to be modified. In the unlikely case
    34	/// data does need to be modified, the caller can make a mutable copy
    35	/// after seeing the error.
    36	///
    37	/// The data is returned as a set of slices to limit allocations. The caller
    38	/// can combine the slices into a single buffer if desired.
    39	///
    40	/// WARNING: The input data is not checked for safety. See the `isSafe`
    41	/// function to check if the data is safe to paste.
    42	pub fn encode(
    43	    data: anytype,
    44	    opts: Options,
    45	) switch (@TypeOf(data)) {
    46	    []u8 => [3][]const u8,
    47	    []const u8 => Error![3][]const u8,
    48	    else => unreachable,
    49	} {
    50	    // These are the set of byte values that are always replaced by
    51	    // a space (per xterm's behavior) for any text insertion method e.g.
    52	    // a paste, drag and drop, etc. These are copied directly from xterm's
    53	    // source.
    54	    const strip: []const u8 = &.{
    55	        0x00, // NUL
    56	        0x08, // BS
    57	        0x05, // ENQ
    58	        0x04, // EOT
    59	        0x1B, // ESC
    60	        0x7F, // DEL
    61	
    62	        // These can be overridden by the running terminal program
    63	        // via tcsetattr, so they aren't totally safe to hardcode like
    64	        // this. In practice, I haven't seen modern programs change these
    65	        // and its a much bigger architectural change to pass these through
    66	        // so for now they're hardcoded.
    67	        0x03, // VINTR (Ctrl+C)
    68	        0x1C, // VQUIT (Ctrl+\)
    69	        0x15, // VKILL (Ctrl+U)
    70	        0x1A, // VSUSP (Ctrl+Z)
    71	        0x11, // VSTART (Ctrl+Q)
    72	        0x13, // VSTOP (Ctrl+S)
    73	        0x17, // VWERASE (Ctrl+W)
    74	        0x16, // VLNEXT (Ctrl+V)
    75	        0x12, // VREPRINT (Ctrl+R)
    76	        0x0F, // VDISCARD (Ctrl+O)
    77	    };

    79	    const mutable = @TypeOf(data) == []u8;
    80	
    81	    var result: [3][]const u8 = .{ "", data, "" };

    83	    // If we have any of the strip values, then we need to replace them
    84	    // with spaces. This is what xterm does and it does it regardless
    85	    // of bracketed paste mode. This is a security measure to prevent pastes
    86	    // from containing bytes that could be used to inject commands.
    87	    if (std.mem.indexOfAny(u8, data, strip) != null) {
    88	        if (comptime !mutable) return Error.MutableRequired;
    89	        var offset: usize = 0;

    91	            u8,
    92	            data[offset..],
    93	            strip,
    94	        )) |idx| {
    95	            offset += idx;
    96	            data[offset] = ' ';
    97	            offset += 1;
    98	        }

   109	    // Non-bracketed. We have to replace newline with `\r`. This matches

   118	    return result;

   127	/// Encode the given data for pasting directly into a writer. This is
   128	/// the same transformation as `encode` (unsafe bytes replaced, bracketed
   129	/// frame or newline conversion per `opts`) but the data is copied
   130	/// exactly once: into the writer's buffer, where it is modified in place.
   131	/// This is the form to use when the data is const and the result is
   132	/// being assembled into a single buffer anyway.
   133	///
   134	/// The data is copied in chunks sized to the writer's buffer, so any
   135	/// writer works; a writer with less total capacity than the writer
   136	/// needs to hold at once reports `error.WriteFailed` as usual.
   137	///
   138	/// WARNING: The input data is not checked for safety. See `isSafe`
   139	/// and `isSafeWith` to check if the data is safe to paste.
   140	pub fn encodeWriter(
   141	    writer: *std.Io.Writer,
   142	    data: []const u8,
   143	    opts: Options,
   144	) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
   145	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_prefix);
   146	
   147	    // The byte transformations are position-independent, so the data
   148	    // can be copied and encoded chunk by chunk. The frame returned by
   149	    // encode is ignored since it's written around the whole data here.
   150	    var remaining = data;
   151	    while (remaining.len > 0) {
   152	        const dest = try writer.writableSliceGreedy(1);
   153	        const n = @min(dest.len, remaining.len);
   154	        @memcpy(dest[0..n], remaining[0..n]);
   155	        _ = encode(dest[0..n], opts);
   156	        writer.advance(n);
   157	        remaining = remaining[n..];
   158	    }
   159	
   160	    if (opts.bracketed) try writer.writeAll(bracketed_suffix);
   161	}
